thesis_summary: PEP has de-rated to the 4th percentile of its 52-week range vs the equal-weight staples basket (z ≈ -1.96) on post-Q2 downgrades and a guidance cut, but the affordability re-investment is showing early volume response and the technical base is turning. Long PEP / short RSPS is a mean-reversion pair with a 4.3% dividend yield floor and sell-side capitulation already in the price.
thesis_detail: PEP trades at a ~4th-percentile ratio vs RSPS (4.4704 as of the 8/7 close: PEP $139.02 / RSPS $31.095) after a -6.8% 3-month slide driven by the mid-July Q2 print: management guided to the low end of the EPS range, leaned heavily on a Q4 ramp, and drew downgrades (Citi Buy→Neutral, target $170→$145; Barclays, Wells Fargo, TD Cowen also cut). That is the consensus position — we are buying after the capitulation, not before it. The variant is that the affordability price investments are working: reporting post-print (Motley Fool, 7/31) indicates price cuts are producing the intended volume response in Frito-Lay North America. Volume-led organic recovery is exactly the decomposition this desk demands — price/mix has been exhausted across staples and PEP is the one name explicitly re-investing for volume. Technicals confirm the inflection: price back above the 20- and 50-day SMAs, RSI 55.5 and rising, MACD histogram positive, +5.3% on the week while XLP was flat. The $5.92 annualized dividend yields ~4.26% at $139, a level that has historically capped downside in this name. KHC's split-pause (announced ~3 weeks ago) and WMT's -10.8% 3-month slide confirm consumer weakness — but both are already consensus, and PEP's pair structure isolates the idiosyncratic recovery from the sector tape. Note: the valuations feed was 429-rate-limited this session, so the multiples leg of the thesis is qualitative; the pair ratio and technicals are computed and fresh.
variant_perception: Consensus just downgraded PEP on guidance risk and back-loaded Q4 delivery. Our variant view: the affordability pivot is producing volume response NOW, the downgrades mark peak pessimism, and a 4th-percentile pair ratio with a 4.3% yield misprices a name whose volume trajectory is inflecting while the sector's pricing-led model is rolling over (KHC split pause, MDLZ -8.6% 1Y).
catalyst: Monthly Nielsen/scanner reads confirming Frito-Lay volume stabilization; Q3 earnings (mid-October) where low-end guidance plus any volume beat forces estimate re-rating; further sell-side capitulation is exhausted, so revisions skew asymmetrically positive from here
catalyst_timeline: 4-8 weeks (scanner data within 2-4 weeks, Q3 print ~8-10 weeks)
key_risks: Q4-loaded guidance is an execution trap — if Q3 shows no volume inflection, the low end of the range gets cut again and the ratio makes new 52-week lows (this is the stop condition)
